localBiteReport: Reports from late July 2026 on the Choctawhatchee Bay/Santa Rosa Beach area show speckled trout as the standout inshore bite, with anglers finding good numbers of fish across the bay despite some wind limiting accessible areas. Redfish have also been active, with a notable bull red (over 26 lbs) landed out of Santa Rosa Beach and guides reporting reds cruising bridges, flats, and the pass on tide movement — live bait like pinfish and finger mullet have been the top producers for both species. The most recent Half Hitch Destin report on record is dated July 13, 2026 (content not fully retrievable), but the broader regional picture from early July shows bay trout biting well on live bait, over-slot reds feeding aggressively in passes and around bridges on falling tides, and at least one recent client trip yielding reds, trout, and a 43-lb black drum. Water temperature is 84°F.

aiSummary: Choctawhatchee Bay is fishing well heading into Monday, with speckled trout the standout bite across the bay and redfish active on tide movement around bridges, flats, and the pass — live pinfish and finger mullet have been the top producers for both species. Winds are light out of the WNW at 0–10 mph, keeping most water accessible, though a 13% storm chance before 4 PM means watching the sky if you push out to the more exposed areas. Get on the water early under the Last Quarter moon and bright sun, target shaded structure and deeper grass edges during midday, and plan to be off open water well before any afternoon build.

bridge.aiNote: The 331 Bridge spans a narrow neck of Choctawhatchee Bay, creating a natural current funnel where bait gets pushed through on both tides. Pilings hold speckled trout, redfish, sheepshead, and black drum year-round, with the lee-side pilings serving as the prime ambush zone on incoming tides. Because it sits on open water, it's the first spot to become unfishable when wind picks up.
bridge.todaysCall: With winds at 0–10 mph WNW today, chop should be minimal and the bridge is fully accessible — take advantage of it. The tide is building toward a late-night high (10:31 PM), so afternoon hours will have a slow but steady incoming push that should stack bait against the pilings. Recent reports have reds cruising bridges on tide movement, so work live pinfish or finger mullet tight to the lee-side pilings during any noticeable current. Keep an eye on the sky since there's a 13% storm chance before 4 PM, and this exposed open-water spot gives you little shelter if weather builds fast — have an exit plan ready.

alaqua.aiNote: Alaqua Bayou offers protected water with a strong year-round redfish population, along with trout and flounder at the mouth. The oyster bars at the creek mouth are the prime structural target, and tree cover keeps the interior a few degrees cooler than the open bay while providing shelter from wind and weather. Upper creek sections transition toward brackish water and can hold bass alongside small reds.
alaqua.todaysCall: Light WNW winds today make the open bay manageable, but Alaqua's tree-lined banks are a genuine asset once the sun gets high and bright — water temperature is already 84°F and full sun will push fish into shaded, cooler edges mid-morning. Work the oyster bars at the mouth during any tide movement ahead of tonight's high; the bay-wide report has reds actively cruising structure on tide push, and live pinfish or finger mullet should produce here. Slightly stained water slightly favors closer presentations — keep baits near the bottom of the oyster bar faces. The protected character of the bayou means you can stay comfortable here even if that sub-4 PM storm chance materializes.

basin.aiNote: Basin Bayou sees less fishing pressure than Alaqua or LaGrange, which tends to produce less-educated fish willing to bite. Interior grass flats are classic sight-fishing territory for redfish in under two feet of water, and pompano can show at the mouth on moving tides in late spring and early summer. It is somewhat less protected than LaGrange if weather builds.
basin.todaysCall: Lower pressure and cooperative fish make Basin Bayou an appealing option on a calm day like today, with winds staying light enough to pole or drift the interior grass flats comfortably. Sight-fish for reds on those shallow flats during the early morning window — bright sun by mid-morning will let you spot tailing or cruising fish, though it also pushes them to shadier edges as the day heats up. The bay-wide report shows reds responding well to live pinfish and finger mullet on tide movement, so match that approach as the tide slowly builds toward tonight's high. With a 13% storm chance before 4 PM and Basin being less sheltered than LaGrange, plan your exit by early afternoon to stay ahead of any weather.

lagrange.aiNote: LaGrange Bayou is the top trout producer among these locations, with legendary oyster bars at the mouth and interior grass flats that hold redfish year-round. Deep holes inside hold black drum and sheepshead, and the bayou offers the most protected water on the north side of the bay — making it the go-to spot when weather threatens. It consistently produces multiple species in a single trip.
lagrange.todaysCall: LaGrange is a strong pick today on multiple fronts: the bay-wide bite has trout and reds both active on live bait, and this is the bay's top trout-producing bayou with oyster structure perfectly suited to that pattern. Start at the mouth oyster bars early while light is low and the tide is still working its way toward tonight's high — any current over those bars will stack bait and draw feeding trout and reds. Slightly stained water calls for natural presentations kept close to structure; live pinfish or finger mullet fished under a popping cork or free-lined along the oyster edges should be productive. If the 13% storm chance before 4 PM develops into anything, LaGrange's protected interior gives you options to stay on the water safely longer than almost any other spot on this list.

fourmile.aiNote: Four Mile Creek is a short tidal creek running between Shipyard Marina and the bay, where tidal flow concentrates redfish and trout in the bends and grass edges on incoming tides. The creek mouth is a prime flounder zone, and the upper section transitions to brackish water that can hold bass alongside small reds. It is the most sheltered fishery in this group and the safest call when weather threatens.
fourmile.todaysCall: With the tide building toward a late-night high, incoming flow will be pushing baitfish up into Four Mile Creek through the afternoon and evening — position in the bends and along grass edges to intercept reds and trout stacking up ahead of that bait push. The creek mouth is worth a few flounder drifts as well, particularly in the slightly stained water where flatfish often hug the bottom near structure. Winds are light today so you won't need the shelter, but Four Mile's short, protected layout means you can fish comfortably here even if that pre-4 PM storm window produces anything. Live finger mullet or pinfish, consistent with the bay-wide top-producing baits, are the right call in this tight-quarters creek environment.

hogtown.aiNote: Hogtown Bayou is a signature Santa Rosa Beach guide spot and one of the most productive trout flats on the bay, with summer mornings being peak time as trout stack on grass in two to four feet of water. Spanish mackerel show at the mouth on moving tides, adding a bonus species to the mix. It sees regular fishing pressure but produces consistently, and its location further from the 331 Bridge means factoring in run time.
hogtown.todaysCall: Get to Hogtown early — this is one of the best-documented summer trout flats on the bay, and the window before full sun is on the water (sunrise 6:02 AM) is when fish are most active on the grass in 2–4 feet. The bay-wide report has trout biting well across the bay on live bait, and Hogtown's grass flat layout is built for exactly that pattern; live pinfish under a popping cork worked along grass edges should be productive. Spanish mackerel at the mouth are a bonus worth a few quick casts on a moving tide before you push inside to the trout. Factor in the longer run time from the 331 Bridge when planning against the pre-4 PM storm window — you want time to fish and still make it back comfortably if weather develops.

mallet.aiNote: Mallet Bayou is a small tributary feeding directly into LaGrange Bayou, this dashboard's top trout producer, just south of Freeport. Its direct connection to LaGrange means the oyster-bar trout-and-redfish pattern that makes LaGrange productive can plausibly extend into this smaller, quieter water. There is far less documented fishing history for Mallet Bayou specifically, but its small, interior character makes it a natural calm-water fallback when wind picks up on the open bay.
mallet.todaysCall: Light winds today mean you don't need Mallet strictly as a weather refuge, but its quiet interior and connection to LaGrange's productive ecosystem make it worth exploring if you want less-pressured water. With the tide building slowly toward tonight's high, tidal exchange between Mallet and LaGrange should create subtle current that concentrates bait along grass edges and any oyster structure present — work these transitions with live pinfish or finger mullet. Expect redfish and trout as the primary targets given the LaGrange connection and the bay-wide report showing both species active on live bait. Treat any fish here as a bonus; if action is slow, LaGrange's well-documented oyster bars are a short move away and likely the more reliable play.

mack.aiNote: Mack Bayou sits on the barrier-island side of Choctawhatchee Bay near Topsail Hill Preserve State Park, well west of the 331 Bridge — a long-run destination rather than a quick local trip. It shares the same protected-bayou character as Alaqua and LaGrange, with marsh grass, oyster bars, and a few interior holes, and sees less pressure simply due to distance. Hewett Bayou and Buck Bayou sit immediately to the east and are realistically fishable in the same trip.
mack.todaysCall: Today's calm conditions — winds 0–10 mph — are exactly the window you want to commit to the longer run out to Mack Bayou; rough weather makes this trip impractical, so use the light air while you have it. Arrive early and work oyster bars and marsh grass edges as the tide builds toward tonight's high, using live pinfish or finger mullet consistent with what's been producing bay-wide for reds and trout. Light pressure on this water means fish are less educated, which can make a meaningful difference in bite quality. With a 13% storm chance before 4 PM, plan your turnaround time conservatively — being this far from the launch when weather builds on open bay water is the main risk of the trip.

hewett.aiNote: Hewett Bayou sits immediately east of Mack Bayou on the barrier-island side of Choctawhatchee Bay near Topsail Hill Preserve State Park, another long-run spot that pairs naturally with Mack and Buck Bayou in a single trip. It shares the same protected-bayou habitat as its neighbors — oyster bars and marsh grass at the mouth with deeper interior holes further in — and benefits from light pressure due to its distance from the main boat ramps.
hewett.todaysCall: Pair Hewett with Mack Bayou today for an efficient long-run trip while calm winds make the crossing comfortable — working both bayous' oyster bars and grass edges covers a lot of productive, low-pressure water in a single outing. As with Mack, the tide building toward tonight's high will create the best current over structural targets like oyster bars at the mouth; time your fishing around any noticeable tide movement for reds and trout. Live bait — pinfish or finger mullet — matches the bay-wide report and is the right approach on this habitat. Same caveat as Mack: with a 13% storm chance before 4 PM, build a conservative return window into your plan before leaving the dock.

buck.aiNote: Buck Bayou is the smallest and least-documented of the three neighboring bayous on the barrier-island side of Choctawhatchee Bay near Topsail Hill Preserve State Park. Its habitat should track its larger neighbors — marsh grass, some oyster structure, and a modest interior — but there is less basis to speak confidently about its productivity. It is best treated as a bonus stop on a Mack and Hewett Bayou trip rather than a standalone destination.
buck.todaysCall: If you're already running west to Mack and Hewett today in the calm conditions, swinging through Buck Bayou adds minimal time and gives you a look at an additional low-pressure stretch of similar habitat. Work any visible oyster structure or grass edges at the mouth during tidal movement with the same live-bait approach producing elsewhere on the bay. Expectations should be modest given the limited fishing history, but less-pressured water occasionally surprises — and today's calm, fishable conditions are exactly when exploring secondary spots makes sense. Keep it a short stop and let Mack and Hewett carry the bulk of your effort on this run.
